title: Boston Trivia Night

questions.q: In which year did the Boston Tea Party take place?
What is the name of the red-brick walking route that links sixteen of Boston's historic sites?
The tall left-field wall at Fenway Park is known by what nickname?
The USS Constitution, berthed in Charlestown, is better known by what nickname?
How many lanterns were hung in the steeple of the Old North Church on the night of Paul Revere's ride?
Which annual race, first run in 1897, finishes on Boylston Street each April?
Boston's nickname "Beantown" comes from which dish, traditionally slow-cooked with molasses?
In Robert McCloskey's picture book Make Way for Ducklings, the duck family settles in which Boston park?
Which river separates Boston from Cambridge?
Which 1980s TV sitcom was set in a Boston bar "where everybody knows your name"?

notes: 16 December 1773; see Boston Tea Party (Wikipedia) or the Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum history pages.
2.5-mile route marked in red brick, 16 official sites; see the Freedom Trail Foundation's own site.
Left-field wall at Fenway Park; see Green Monster (Wikipedia) or MLB.com's Red Sox ballpark pages.
USS Constitution, nicknamed Old Ironsides in the War of 1812, berthed at Charlestown Navy Yard; see the USS Constitution Museum.
Two lanterns signalled the British were crossing by water ('one if by land, two if by sea'); see the Old North Church's own history pages.
First Boston Marathon 19 April 1897, finish line on Boylston Street; see the Boston Athletic Association (baa.org).
Boston baked beans with molasses gave the city the name Beantown; see Boston baked beans (Wikipedia).
The Mallards settle in the Public Garden lagoon, with bronze statues there since 1987; see Make Way for Ducklings (Wikipedia).
The Charles River divides Boston and Cambridge; see Charles River (Wikipedia) or the Charles River Watershed Association.
Cheers (NBC, 1982-1993), set in a Boston bar, theme 'Where Everybody Knows Your Name'; see Cheers (Wikipedia).
